Shape.Name: Procedure
Shape.Text:
If distortion is seen only in EPI acquisitions it is most likely due to inadequate eddy current compensation
EPI image quality and specifically Diffusion Weighted Echo Planar Imaging (DW-EPI) is very sensitive to gradient performance The accuracy of the gradient fields will have a commanding effect on distortion of the image. Because DWEPI is inherently extremely demanding on the gradient subsystem the significance of accurate eddy current compensation is greatly increased
Please refer to Diffusion Weighted Echo Planar Image Quality (DWEPIQ) for additional details.

Shape.Name: Create request
Shape.Text: Review several similar patient scans and look for the same type or anatomical area of distortion. NOTE: If the distortion is patient dependent it will not be seen in the same anatomical region of multiple patients. Also, it will most likely be localized

Shape.Name: Procedure
Shape.Text:
If distortion is not seen on other patients using the same or similar protocol, it is safe to assume the distortion was patient dependent.
Materials known to cause shading : Patient implanted metal Mascara Make-up Hearing Aids Oral Bridgework, excessive cavities Some form of tattoos "Spandex" clothing "Slimfast" diet drink or a vitamin B injection
These items may distort the magnetic field or the transmitted RF field in a small area surrounding the item. This small field disturbance can create a distorted image.

Shape.Name: Procedure
Shape.Text: Image problems caused by gradients are most easily seen when in the frequency or phase encoding directions. Changing encoding direction, scan planes or selected coil type will switch the suspected bad axis to perform in the other encoding functions. Once distortion is observed do not change scan planes or coils, this might make the suspected amplifier the slice select gradient and the distortion will not be evident in the image If the image distortion is in one direction i.e. left to right (Body, Axial Scan, Frequency encode on X Gradient amplifier) and a new swap Phase/Frequency scan is done (Body, Axial Scan, Frequency encode on Y Gradient amplifier) and the distortion changes top to bottom the failure is within the SRF / TRF.

Shape.Name: Create request
Shape.Text:
When troubleshooting Geometric distortion it is strongly recommended to use the DQA phantom for imaging. The DQA dimensions are known and the internal structures make it easy to determine the direction or axis of distortion
1. Change the scan prescription to move the suspected bad axis (amplifier) to a different encoding function (either frequency or phase). This is done on the ACQUISITION TIME section, select the opposite FREQUENCY DIRECTION. Rescan and observe the resulting image
2. Based on the results of the previous step if distortion in the image did change with the change in functions, click on this box to see how to run the MGD Diagnostics tool and follow the flowchart to AGP Diagnostics.
If the distortion did not follow the change in gradient functions, continue the flow to isolate the amplifier. In other words if the original image was squashed left to right and the swap Phase / Frequency image is now squashed top to bottom then answer yes and proceed to MGD diagnostics. If both images are squashed left to right answer no and proceed to next step. Once the distortion is observed in a particular plane, use the following matrix to correlate the failing image plane to the suspected bad axis.

Shape.Name: Procedure.11
Shape.Text: All of the Slice, Phase and Frequency encoding functions, including Oblique Plane Imaging, are routed to the proper gradient amplifier from the SRF / TRF board. The SRF / TRF board passes the serial data ( GDATX , GDATY , GDATZ ) to the STIF board for fiber optics conversion and is then sent to each respective amplifier. For the distortion to follow the encoding function the problem is within the AGP board.

Shape.Name: Procedure.18
Shape.Text: Every gradient pulse causes some movement of the wires in the magnetic field. This movement can cause the wires to fray and lead to shorts between the wires or opens in a single wire. Either can cause severe distortion (collapsed image), ghosting or white pixel / corduroy artifacts and usually produces Current Distortion Faults. Inspecting the cabling and measuring the resistance helps isolates the problem to either the coil and gradient pigtail or the cable path from the gradient amp to the rear pedestal.
